messages:
sarah: deploybot flagged the canary build with an SBOM ambiguity on tinyhttp (third-party). :eyes:

deploybot: SBOM scan summary:
```
package: tinyhttp
version: 0.3.1
license: UNKNOWN / ambiguous
provenance: unsigned
vuln: none detected
policy: requires_explicit_approval (security_level: medium)
```

ranjit: medium risk because ambiguous license can be a legal exposure depending on redistribution. any idea if this is direct or transitive?

micah: transitive via authn-lib -> http-layer -> tinyhttp. quick tree shows it only used in dev/test harness, but it ended up in the image because of build tooling.

ops_tom: can we rebuild without it? quick patch: replace build step to use curl-wrapper v1.2 which doesn't pull tinyhttp. would be a minor build change.

jen: timeline? we have a scheduled change window at 18:00 PT. canary needs to go out before that or we delay.

legal: we need evidence to approve. if it's only in non-prod tooling, low appetite to block. but we need a written exception or a pin with mitigation.

ranjit: options: 1) pin to known-good digest of tinyhttp v0.3.0 (older license checked) 2) rebuild to drop it 3) proceed with a restricted canary (EU-only, 10%) + monitoring + followup remediation.

sarah: quick cost/ops call: rebuilding will take ~40m and a redeploy. pin is fastest (but still needs verif). restricted canary seems OK if legal signs off on exception and we file remediation ticket.

deploybot: suggested action: `hold = true` unless approving user in group @sec-approvers sets `hold=false`. Current state: hold=true.

sarah: @ranjit can you review the evidence and give a short approval comment if you think EU-only limited rollout is acceptable?

ranjit: I can sign a conditional approve: EU-only canary 10% for 2 hours, require rollback if any anomaly. Will sign once ops confirms mitigation and ticket exists. :white_check_mark:

ops_tom: started the patch branch to replace the build dependency (will still take ~30m). but also prepared a pin fallback. commands I'm going to run:
```bash
# pin tinyhttp to v0.3.0 digest in build matrix
ci/replace-dep tinyhttp@0.3.0 --pin-digest sha256:abcd1234
# or promote canary restricted
deployctl promote --env canary --region eu --traffic 10
```

micah: I will watch canary for exceptions and run quick end-to-end smoke for tokenization and auth. alert channels ready.

legal: I will sign the temporary exception if the canary is limited to EU and a remediation ticket exists with ETA < 72h.

jen: adding to release notes: "Staged canary: feature X; temporary SBOM ambiguity on tinyhttp (transitive) — limited EU rollout, remediation planned."

sarah: decision: perform EU-only 10% canary now with deploybot hold cleared after @ranjit posts approval. ops will run pin fallback in parallel and submit remediation ticket RN-4821.

ranjit: posted approval comment: "conditional approve: EU-only 10% for 2h, monitor, rollback on anomalies. remediation ticket RN-4821 created." :white_check_mark:

deploybot: hold cleared by ranjit. kicking EU canary (10%).

ops_tom: running: `deployctl promote --env canary --region eu --traffic 10`

micah: smoke ok so far, no auth regressions in first 5m. metrics dashboard: https://internal.redwood/metrics/build/1234 :thumbsup:

legal: documented exception attached to RN-4821.

sarah: pinned fallback branch pushed and CI started (pin tinyhttp@0.3.0 digest). if canary sees issues we will switch traffic to fallback build and open a postmortem.

jen: updated release notes and changelog entry. preparing a short customer-facing blurb in case of rollback.

sarah: 1704509955 — EU canary running, monitoring green, remediation ticket exists. closing thread for now; anyone escalating ping me. :rocket:
